newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn sees coal pact leading to energy consensus.
newsitem.headline: Bonn sees coal pact leading to energy consensus.

text.p: The coal subsidies deal reached on Thursday could open the way to a broader consensus with opposition Social Democrats (SPD) on other controversial energy policy issues, government spokesman Peter Hausmann said.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition believes "on the basis of the results reached so far (it can) also come to an understanding on nuclear power plants and waste storage," Hausmann said in a statement.
The SPD agreed on Thursday to hold a fresh round of talks on energy policy next week, Hausmann said.

The SPD wants Germany to end its reliance on nuclear power, while the Kohl government wants it to continue. Attempts in past years to resolve those differences -- which linked the coal and nuclear issues -- ended in failure, but the government hopes at least to achieve an agreement on what to do with Germany's nuclear waste.
That could help prevent repeats of the recent violent confrontation between anti-nuclear demonstrators and police at the Gorleben waste dump.
